records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is a small basic secondary amine with a primary carboxamide; the closest reference, pramipexole, shares the tetrahydro-fused bicyclic amine scaffold and has accepted absolute oral bioavailability >90% despite full ionization at physiological pH (C01), with measurable oral exposure after extended-release dosing (C76).

Other ionized small-molecule references exceed the 20% threshold: 5-HTP 49% (C11), labetalol 33% in controls and 63% in cirrhosis (C13, C16, C17, C24), AZD0837 22-55% (C04, C05, C14, C20), ebastine ~40% (C02), and PF-05241328 38% (C03, C08).

L4 solubility records for basic/primary-amide compounds show high aqueous solubility at low pH (galunisertib 4.81 mg/mL at pH 2.65, C129; >=20 mg/mL at pH<3, C115; 4.811 mg/mL at pH 2, C100) and small basic drugs can be freely soluble (C128), supporting that ionization does not preclude dissolution.

The only below-threshold measured F among reference contexts is isradipine's non-cirrhotic baseline of 16% (C22), but it is condition-specific and structurally dissimilar (dihydropyridine ester), so it does not transfer to the query.

The L4 permeability caution (low passive PAMPA for a different larger indole amide, C109) is not a query measurement and does not affirmatively establish F<20%, especially since active transport can mediate absorption of ionized small molecules.
